text: The predicate asks whether finitely many vectors span the underlying R-module. It puts no bound on the number of elements and selects no basis; over a field it means finite dimension. This matches [Stacks, Definition 10.5.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0517); the source makes precisely this predicate the object property of right comodules. Checks pass: [isFG_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L67), [finite_zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L82).
Unfolds the object property to Module.Finite on the same carrier.
The zero comodule supplies the zero-generator boundary case.

Objects are right comodules together with finite generation of their underlying modules; every coaction-preserving linear map remains a morphism. Thus this is the full subcategory described by [Stacks, Definition 4.2.10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001D), specialized over fields to finite-dimensional comodules. Finite generation neither chooses a basis nor asserts projectivity over a general semiring. Checks pass: [isFG_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L67), [ofHom_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L193).
Confirms the precise finite-generation object predicate.
Confirms that full-subcategory composition is the original comodule composition.

This projection returns the underlying elements of the already stored comodule. It imposes no extra subset or quotient: finite generation is attached as a proof about that same module. This is the object-plus-property construction of a [full subcategory](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001D); the source reuses the ambient carrier exactly. Checks pass: [of_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L157), [ofHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L203).
Bundling and projecting recovers the original ambient comodule.
A bundled morphism acts on precisely the original elements.

Writing an object M as a type means taking its underlying carrier, so a variable of type M is an ordinary comodule element. The finite-generation proof does not become part of each element. The definition simply installs this projection for the [full-subcategory construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001D), as confirmed by the unchanged object and morphism evaluations. Checks pass: [of_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L157), [ofHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L203).
The carrier comes from the same ambient object.
Elementwise application recovers the original unbundled map.

Addition and zero on a finitely generated comodule are inherited from its ambient comodule without modification. Additive inverses are not required over the commutative semiring base. This preserves the algebraic object when imposing the [full-subcategory restriction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001D); bundling and forgetting keep the same additive module and its maps. Checks pass: [forget₂_semimoduleCat_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L136), [ofHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L203).
Forgetting gives the identical ambient semimodule object.
Bundled morphisms retain their original elementwise action.

Scalar multiplication by R is the one already stored on the ambient comodule. The finite-generation property adds no new scalar action and no basis choice. This is the underlying-module component of the [full-subcategory construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001D); the forgetful object equation and original coaction equation confirm that both structures use the same module. Checks pass: [forget₂_semimoduleCat_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L136), [of_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L163).
Forgetting exposes the unchanged module structure.
Bundling preserves the coaction on that module.

The finite object carries its original right coaction ρ:M→M⊗C, with the original coassociativity and counit laws. No coaction is reconstructed from generators. The equations match [EGNO, Definition 1.20.2](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41) over fields, and the source inherits this structure unchanged over commutative semirings. Checks pass: [of_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L163), [corestrict_obj_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Corestrict.lean#L79).
The finite bundle has exactly the supplied coaction.
A downstream coefficient change uses that same coaction before applying id⊗f.

This instance extracts the finite-generation proof stored with the object. In [Stacks, Definition 10.5.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0517), finiteness means a finite spanning family; it does not mean a finite set of elements. The source returns the existing property directly, so no choice of generators or stronger freeness assertion is introduced. Checks pass: [isFG_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L67), [finite_zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L82).
Identifies the stored property with module finite generation.
Checks the zero object satisfies this finiteness convention.

The inclusion forgets only the finite-generation proof, sending each finite comodule and each morphism to its ambient counterpart. This is the usual fully faithful inclusion of a [full subcategory](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001D). Its native corestriction compatibility equations confirm that neither the carrier nor the underlying coaction-preserving map is altered. Checks pass: [incl_corestrict_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Corestrict.lean#L110), [incl_corestrict_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Corestrict.lean#L120).
Inclusion commutes with coefficient corestriction on objects.
Inclusion commutes with coefficient corestriction on morphisms.

This forgetful functor first drops the finite-generation proof and then the coaction, retaining the underlying R-semimodule and linear maps. It is ordinary composition of [functors in Stacks, Definition 4.2.8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0013). Semimodule allows an additive monoid over a semiring; additive inverses and any choice of finite generators are unnecessary. Checks pass: [forget₂_semimoduleCat_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L136), [forget₂_semimoduleCat_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L144).
Identifies its object with the ambient forgetful object.
Identifies its morphism with the ambient underlying linear map.

Given a right coaction and finite generation of its underlying module, this constructor bundles exactly those data. The coaction has the meaning of [EGNO, Definition 1.20.2](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41), and finite generation is supplied as a hypothesis rather than inferred from the coalgebra. The object and coaction equations show that bundling changes neither. Checks pass: [of_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L157), [of_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L163).
The ambient object is the original bundled comodule.
The resulting coaction is the supplied unbundled coaction.

A coaction-preserving linear map between finitely generated comodules becomes a categorical morphism by keeping that map. There is no extra finiteness condition on its image or fibres. This realizes the morphism equality required for a [full subcategory](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001D); the identity and composition laws agree with the original comodule operations. Checks pass: [ofHom_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L187), [ofHom_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L193).
Bundling respects the identity comodule map.
Bundling respects composition in the correct order.

A linear equivalence becomes a comodule isomorphism when its forward map intertwines the coactions. Applying its inverse on the module tensor factor proves inverse compatibility; the finite full subcategory then inherits both maps. This matches [categorical isomorphisms, Stacks 4.2.4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0013) and does not mistake an arbitrary linear equivalence for a comodule isomorphism. Checks pass: [isoOfLinearEquiv_hom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L225), [isoOfLinearEquiv_inv_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L235).
The forward morphism is the given linear equivalence.
The inverse morphism is its actual inverse linear map.

The tensor product uses the diagonal right coaction (m⊗n)↦Σ(m₀⊗n₀)⊗m₁n₁ of [EGNO §1.21, p. 44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). Pairwise tensors of finite spanning vectors span the tensor product, so it remains finitely generated. A bialgebra suffices; its coefficient multiplication need not commute, and the displayed order m₁n₁ is retained. Checks pass: [tensor_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/TensorProduct.lean#L79), [tensorMap_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/TensorProduct.lean#L124).
Identifies the selected coaction with the native diagonal tensor coaction.
Checks the tensor construction on morphisms and simple tensors.

Tensoring comodule morphisms sends m⊗n to f(m)⊗g(n). Their coaction compatibility makes this map compatible with the ordered diagonal coaction in [EGNO §1.21, p. 44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). The finite wrapper adds no further condition; native identity and composition equations show the operation is functorial for bialgebras over commutative semirings. Checks pass: [tensorMap_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/TensorProduct.lean#L130), [tensorMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/TensorProduct.lean#L137).
Tensoring identities gives the tensor-object identity.
Tensoring respects both component compositions.

A coalgebra map f:C→D changes a right coaction to (id⊗f)ρ while leaving the module and every underlying linear map unchanged. Preservation of coproduct and counit ensures the [right-comodule equations of EGNO 1.20.2](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). Hence finite generation is inherited directly; f need not be injective or surjective. Checks pass: [corestrict_obj_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Corestrict.lean#L79), [corestrict_map_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Corestrict.lean#L104).
Evaluates the new coaction as id⊗f after the original coaction.
Confirms the underlying function of every morphism is unchanged.

This functor sends M to A⊗_R M and a comodule morphism to id_A⊗f, the usual [tensor-product operation](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). Its target consists of A-semimodules, without a specified coaction. The source restricts the ambient functor to finitely generated objects; A may be noncommutative, and no flatness hypothesis is needed for functoriality. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L65), [scalarExtensionFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L71).
Identifies the object with A⊗R M.
Identifies the morphism with base change of its underlying linear map.

The equality says that scalar extension on finite comodules is obtained by first including them among all comodules, then applying the ambient functor M↦A⊗_R M. This is [functor composition, Stacks 4.2.8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0013), directly as defined. It restricts the domain; it does not claim a new coaction or reconstruction theorem. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L65), [scalarExtensionFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L71).
Checks the restricted functor on objects.
Checks the restricted functor on morphisms.

The value at M is exactly the A-semimodule A⊗_R M, with A acting on the first tensor factor. This is scalar extension through the [tensor-product universal construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV), without asserting injectivity of m↦1⊗m. The finite-comodule wrapper only restricts inputs, and the source reduces this equation to the ambient functor. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ScalarExtension.lean#L63), [scalarExtensionFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L71).
The ambient functor has the stated tensor-product object.
The associated morphism equation uses precisely these object identifications.

On simple tensors the morphism is a⊗m↦a⊗f(m), the [tensor-induced linear map](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). The displayed equality transports merely identify equal bundled A-semimodules on either side; they do not add a mathematical map. The source reduces to ambient scalar extension, with no flatness or commutativity assumption on A. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/ScalarExtension.lean#L69), [scalarExtensionFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L65).
The ambient morphism equation gives base change with the same transports.
Checks the source and target object identifications.

A family of invertible A-linear maps on A⊗_R M determines a functor automorphism when it commutes with every scalar-extended comodule morphism. These are exactly the [naturality squares in Stacks 4.2.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0013); the inverse maps give the inverse transformation. Tensor-product compatibility is not assumed, so the construction concerns ordinary natural automorphisms. Checks pass: [autOfComponents_hom_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L116), [autOfComponents_inv_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L131).
The forward component is the supplied automorphism after object identification.
The inverse component is its actual inverse after the same identification.

The assembled automorphism acts on each object by the originally supplied linear automorphism. The equality maps in the formula only identify the functor value with A⊗_R M. This is componentwise assembly of a [natural transformation, Stacks 4.2.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0013); inspecting the definition confirms that no basis choice or additional conjugation is inserted. Checks pass: [autOfComponents_inv_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L131), [autOfComponents_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L167).
The inverse component uses the corresponding inverse family.
Assembly respects pointwise composition of families.

If F and G commute with every scalar-extended comodule morphism, so does their product: move the morphism successively past F and G. Here FG means F∘G, applying G first. This is the componentwise [composition law for natural transformations, Stacks 4.2.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0013), proved directly without tensor-compatibility assumptions. Checks pass: [autOfComponents_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L167).
Uses the proved naturality to assemble the product family into the product automorphism.

Assembling the pointwise products F(M)G(M) gives the product of the assembled natural automorphisms, matching [componentwise composition, Stacks 4.2.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0013). Both products apply G first, then F. Lean writes categorical composition in the opposite textual order, and its Aut multiplication compensates for this; cancelling the object identifications proves the equation. Checks pass: [autOfComponents_hom_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L116), [autOfComponents_inv_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L131).
Exposes the forward components used to compare the two products.
Confirms that the assembled objects are genuine automorphisms with inverse components.

Pointwise equal families give the same natural automorphism, because a [natural transformation is determined by its components, Stacks 4.2.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0013). The proof compares those components after the identical object identifications. Different proofs that the families are natural supply no additional mathematical data and therefore do not affect the resulting automorphism. Checks pass: [autOfComponents_hom_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Basic.lean#L116).
Reduces equality of assembled forward transformations to equality of their supplied components.

Including a finite sum of nonnegative real numbers in [0,∞] gives the same result as including each summand and then summing. No infinity can arise from this finite collection of finite inputs. The empty collection is included: its sum is zero on both sides. No conditions are imposed on values outside the indexing set. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/BigOperators.lean#L32).

Converting a finite real product to [0,∞] agrees with multiplying the converted factors when every indexed factor is nonnegative. The empty product is one on both sides. The sign restriction prevents two negative factors from producing a positive product before conversion while each factor is clipped to zero when converted separately. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/BigOperators.lean#L59).

For a finite family of nonnegative real numbers, conversion to [0,∞] commutes with summation. Only indexed terms need be nonnegative, and the empty sum is zero. Without the sign assumptions, positive and negative terms can cancel before conversion: 1+(−1) converts to zero, whereas the separately clipped terms sum to one. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/BigOperators.lean#L118).

A finite product of finite extended nonnegative values is strictly below infinity. Zero factors are allowed, and the empty product is one, hence finite. The converse is not asserted: a product containing both zero and infinity is zero under this arithmetic, so a finite product need not have every factor finite. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/BigOperators.lean#L88).

If every factor in a finite indexed product differs from infinity, the product also differs from infinity. This expresses finiteness as “not infinity” rather than “strictly below infinity”. It includes an empty product, equal to one. A zero factor can make a product finite even with an infinite factor, so no converse is claimed. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/BigOperators.lean#L85).

A finite sum of extended nonnegative values is finite exactly when every indexed summand is finite. Unlike multiplication, addition cannot remove infinity: a single infinite summand makes the sum infinite. For an empty indexing set, the sum is zero and the condition on all summands is vacuous, so the equivalence still holds. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/BigOperators.lean#L94).

Converting a finite product of extended nonnegative values to a real equals multiplying their converted values, without excluding infinity. An infinite factor makes the extended product either infinity or zero; both convert to zero, matching the zero converted factor. The empty product is one, and conversion preserves that unit. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/BigOperators.lean#L55).

Converting a finite sum to a real agrees with summing the converted values when every summand is finite. The empty sum is included. Finiteness prevents the infinity-to-zero default from breaking additivity: the sum ∞+1 converts to zero, but converting the two terms first gives 0+1=1. This is a finite-sum statement. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/BigOperators.lean#L113).

Left multiplication by any extended nonnegative value commutes with arbitrary suprema, including the empty supremum zero. Zero multipliers give zero on both sides. For an infinite multiplier, either every family value is zero or some value is positive; these cases give zero or infinity respectively, so no finiteness hypothesis on the multiplier is needed. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L816).

Right multiplication by a fixed extended nonnegative value commutes with the supremum of any family. No nonzero, finiteness, or nonempty-family assumption is required. In particular, the empty supremum is zero and 0·∞=0, so even an infinite multiplier preserves it. Commutativity gives this right-hand version from the corresponding left multiplication identity. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L827).

The supremum of a family of extended nonnegative values equals zero exactly when every value equals zero. This relies on zero being the least element; there are no negative values whose supremum could be zero. Empty families are included: their supremum is zero, and the condition on every member is vacuously true. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L637).

The supremum of all natural numbers, viewed as extended nonnegative reals, is infinity. Each individual natural number is finite, but there is no finite upper bound for the entire family. This is the Archimedean unboundedness statement expressed in a complete ordered domain; it does not mean that any natural number itself is infinite. Compared with [Kiming Theorem 3(1–2)](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L641).

The supremum of a family constantly equal to zero is zero in the extended nonnegative reals, regardless of the indexing type. The family need not contain an index: the empty supremum is also zero because zero is the least element. This differs from the empty infimum, whose value in the same domain is infinity. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L639).

If every sum formed from two nonempty indexed subfamilies is at most a, the sum of their suprema is also at most a. The subfamilies are selected by predicates, and infinite values are allowed. Nonemptiness matters: otherwise the pairwise bound can be vacuous while the remaining family’s supremum still exceeds a. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L677).

The sum of two extended nonnegative values is infinity exactly when at least one summand is infinity. Two finite values cannot produce infinity, and an infinite summand is absorbed into an infinite sum. This concerns ordinary extended addition, with no negative infinity available to create an indeterminate cancellation. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L151).

A sum of two extended nonnegative values differs from infinity exactly when both summands differ from infinity. Here “not infinity” means finite, including zero. This equivalence works because finite real addition stays finite and infinity absorbs addition; it is stronger than the corresponding sufficient condition for multiplication, where a zero factor can absorb infinity. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L179).

A sum of two extended nonnegative values is strictly below infinity precisely when both summands are strictly below infinity. Since infinity is the greatest element, these strict inequalities simply express finiteness; they do not impose a particular finite upper bound. Zero summands are allowed, while either infinite summand makes the sum infinite. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L153).

Every finite extended nonnegative value is strictly smaller than some natural number included in the same domain. This is the ordinary Archimedean property, with the finiteness assumption excluding infinity, which no natural number exceeds. The witness is automatically positive because the original value is nonnegative and the comparison is strict. Compared with [Kiming Theorem 3(1–2)](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L623).

Every nonzero extended nonnegative value exceeds the reciprocal of some natural number. This includes infinity; for positive finite inputs it is the usual arbitrarily small reciprocal property. Although the natural witness is not explicitly required positive, zero cannot work: the reciprocal of its cast is infinity, which is never strictly below another value. Compared with [Kiming Theorem 3(1–2)](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L651).

An extended nonnegative value that is at least every finite nonnegative real must be infinity. This characterizes the added top element using finite comparison values. If the value were finite, a larger finite real, such as its value plus one, would contradict the hypothesis. The quantifier ranges over all nonnegative reals, not merely a bounded subset. Compared with [Kiming Theorem 3(1–2)](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L503).

For a differentiable real function f on a finite-dimensional manifold with nondegenerate two-form σ, this is the unique vector field satisfying σ(X_f,v)=df(v), with the positive-df sign. The definition also accepts arbitrary data: a noninvertible flat map or a nondifferentiability point gives zero. Closedness of σ is unnecessary for this construction. See [Cannas da Silva, §18.1, p.105](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~acannas/Papers/lsg.pdf). Native Checks pass: [The contraction equation characterizes the field](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Hamiltonian/Manifold.lean#L207), [The actual constant-form field agrees with the linear construction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Hamiltonian/Manifold.lean#L232), [C^(n+1) Hamiltonians give C^n fields](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Hamiltonian/Manifold.lean#L215), [Energy is constant on an open preconnected time set](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Hamiltonian/Manifold.lean#L112). The [canonical cotangent pairing](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Cotangent/StrongDual.lean#L88) fixes the coordinate signs in that constant-form family.
The contraction equation characterizes the field
The actual constant-form field agrees with the linear construction
C^(n+1) Hamiltonians give C^n fields
Energy is constant on an open preconnected time set

On a finite-dimensional real manifold, this assigns tangent vectors the value [JX,JY]−[X,Y]−J[JX,Y]−J[X,JY] of differentiable extensions. Tensoriality proves independence of those extensions, giving a continuous bilinear map on each tangent space. The bracket is the usual commutator of derivations, and no factor ¼ is included. Smoothness and J²=−1 are assumed; integrability is not. See [Cannas da Silva, Homework10, p.82](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~acannas/Papers/lsg.pdf). Native Checks pass: [The tensor evaluates to the four-term bracket expression](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Manifold/Nijenhuis.lean#L151), [Applying J gives the required negative-J sign](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Manifold/Nijenhuis.lean#L199), [Every constant almost complex structure has zero tensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Manifold/Nijenhuis.lean#L242).
